correctness.rationale: The proof states normalized finite and infinite Fourier conventions, exact domains, all parameters and Baire quantifiers. Nielsen Theorem 2.1 and its proof were materially inspected as the published complex input. The new phase coordinate gives disjoint +1/-1 Fourier slices for odd p and the exact threshold identity. Averaging squared real parts gives an >=1/p phase chance per complex good point. Independent coordinate blocks and strict magnitude separation give a real finite model with arbitrarily high good measure, and regular thresholds make the real Banach Baire sets open and dense. The separate infinite block construction, summable norm and second Borel-Cantelli prove finite spectral avoidance and a.e. divergence. The delivered checker tests new finite identities only (120 regular thresholds and two-block separation); infinite statements rely on proof, not experiments.

value.rationale: The complex-to-real restriction is structurally nontrivial for nonlinear magnitude-level threshold summation: taking real parts can alter coefficient magnitudes and change the selected sets. The exact two-slice lemma avoids that issue, while independent-coordinate probability amplification proves a full dense G_delta and a.e. divergence for real signals in a natural nonbinary compact Fourier system. This answers a mathematically motivated real-data variant, not a routine finite or arbitrary parameter substitution.
